summary: Use a Note Input for a short, optional memo under an amount, such as “Rent for April”, that grows as people type.

avoidWhen.text: A detail people must give, such as a reason for the transfer: Note Input has no label, required mark, or error, so people skip it. Ask for it in a Form Field, whose label and required mark say it must be filled in.

examples.purpose: A memo under the transfer amount, the guide's In context: a Card titled for the person, an AmountInput with the amount first and the NoteInput under it, and the payment Button. The note keeps what people type on its own, and onChangeText gives the screen each change, so the screen keeps both values and sends the note with the payment. AmountInput carries Context3 Amount Input, which the guide's own source sets on it, because it doesn't set its own context and passes its modes to both of its children; nothing else sets modes.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <Card.Title>Send to Asha Rao</Card.Title>
  <AmountInput
    modes={{ Context3: 'Amount Input' }}
    moneyValueSlot={<MoneyValue value="500" currency="₹" />}
    noteInputSlot={<NoteInput onChangeText={(note) => {}} />}
  />
  <Button label="Send ₹500" onPress={() => {}} />
</Card>

from.quote: The screen keeps both values and sends the note with the payment.

props.name: value
props.description: Optional. Without it the note keeps its own state and takes typing; with it the screen owns the note (value and onChangeText). Declared: The value of the text input.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The placeholder when empty ("Add note" by default) Default "Add note", from the component source.

props.name: state
props.description: Not a designer variant: state Editing only hides the placeholder. Focus clears the placeholder on its own. Declared: State of the component.

props.name: ...Omit<TextInputProps, 'style' | 'value' | 'onChangeText' | 'placeholder'>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: The note's spoken name (on the web, the field's aria-label). Without it the placeholder names the note, and the name stays while the placeholder is hidden on focus.

props.name: editable
props.description: false makes the note read only: the background is at 60% opacity, the field is read-only and out of the tab order, a click doesn't focus it, and it keeps its placeholder.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Limits how many characters people can type; there is no counter.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Ignored: the note doesn't start from it. To start with a note, pass value and update it from onChangeText.
